subject.title: fix(sessions): keep dirty transcript search from blocking the gateway

question: Should dirty transcript reconciliation permanently use the proposed database claim-generation encoding, process-wide single-slot worker queue, and planning/progress watchdog policy?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but these choices define persistent session-state and operational recovery semantics rather than a purely mechanical event-loop fix.

options.title: Adopt this lifecycle
options.body: Accept the database claim generation, serialized worker queue, and watchdog values as the canonical dirty-index reconciliation contract.

options.title: Narrow the worker contract
options.body: Keep reconciliation off the Gateway thread but request a simpler or separately modeled claim and scheduling design before merge.

options.title: Pause for storage redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until transcript-index ownership and rebuild state receive a broader schema-level design review.

recommendation.title: Adopt this lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the database claim generation, serialized worker queue, and watchdog values as the canonical dirty-index reconciliation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only evidence-backed person available who has worked across the full reconciliation, mutation, packaging, and proof surface; a repository owner should make the final acceptance decision if another session-storage owner is available.
